text: If you ever fake a number, there's a way to tell a human made it up.
A man stole two million dollars with fake checks,
made every amount look totally random and still got caught.
Well, picture a building with 19 floors.
Step into the elevator and look at the buttons.
Floor's two through nine each start with a different number,
but floor one and ten all the way up to 19 all start with a one.
That's more than half the buttons.
Real numbers work like that elevator,
so ones show up way more than anything else.
On top of that, real randomness is streaky.
Flip a coin a hundred times,
and you'll usually get six heads in a row.
His checks mostly began with a seven, eight or nine,
and he avoided doubles to make them look random,
but truly random numbers are the opposite.
So no matter how random you try to make yours,
there's almost always a way to tell.
